charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Domestic stock revenue growth slowed down to 13% YoY
charts.commentary: Domestic stock revenue growth slowed to 13% YoY in 4QFY26 from 20-25% levels seen in prior years, signalling a deceleration in India's nominal demand cycle that warrants caution on volume-sensitive cyclicals.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: International stock revenue grew 10% YoY
charts.commentary: International-facing stocks (IT, pharma, metals) delivered 10% revenue growth in 4QFY26, slightly below domestic peers, suggesting global demand softness has not yet caused a sharp deceleration but leaves limited upside for export-driven names.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Domestic stock Ebitda growth declined to 9% YoY
charts.commentary: Domestic EBITDA growth dropped to 9% from double-digit revenue growth, with the margin gap widening — a red flag for earnings quality and a signal that operating leverage is not materialising as expected in this cycle.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: International stock Ebitda growth stood at 8% YoY
charts.commentary: International stocks' EBITDA growth of 8% broadly matched revenue growth at 10%, implying flat margins versus domestic peers where cost pressure is more acute — pharma and IT are the relatively more margin-stable cohorts.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Domestic stock PBT growth stood at 11% YoY
charts.commentary: Domestic PBT growth of 11% YoY outpaced EBITDA growth of 9%, likely aided by lower financing costs and other income; nonetheless this is below the 15-16% expectation at the season's start, confirming the domestic earnings disappointment narrative.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: International stock PBT growth was flat YoY
charts.commentary: International-facing stocks saw flat PBT YoY — a stark contrast to domestic peers — with the chart showing significant volatility in prior quarters driven by commodity cycles; the flat print signals an earnings trough for this cohort that could be a contrarian positive.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Consumption stock revenue growth rose to 22% YoY
charts.commentary: Consumption plays delivered 22% revenue growth in 4QFY26, accelerating sharply versus prior quarters and outpacing investment stocks — a positive signal for the consumer-led recovery thesis, though much of it may be price-led.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Investment stocks revenue growth remained at 12%YoY
charts.commentary: Investment-cycle stocks maintained a steady 12% revenue growth in 4QFY26, consistent with the prior few quarters; the absence of acceleration despite government capex push suggests order execution lags are still weighing on reported revenues.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Consumption stock Ebitda growth saw slight uptick
charts.commentary: Consumption EBITDA growth ticked up slightly in 4QFY26 after several quarters of compression, suggesting early signs of margin recovery as input cost tailwinds from softer commodities begin filtering through the P&L.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Investment stock Ebitda growth moderated sharply to 1% YoY
charts.commentary: Investment stock EBITDA growth collapsed to just 1% YoY, the weakest in several years, pointing to severe margin squeeze in capital goods, EMS and infrastructure names — an earnings risk that the market has not fully priced in.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Domestic stock PBT growth stood at 24% YoY
charts.commentary: Consumption plays' PBT surged 24% YoY, well above EBITDA growth, likely reflecting non-operating income and lower financing costs; the strong PBT print contrasts with still-compressed EBITDA and points to quality-of-earnings questions.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Investment stock PBT growth was flat YoY
charts.commentary: Investment stocks delivered flat PBT growth in 4QFY26, confirming that capex-cycle names are in an earnings trough; unless order inflows and execution improve materially, FY27 estimates for capital goods and infra remain at downgrade risk.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Rural stocks revenue growth marginally stood at 19% YoY
charts.commentary: Rural-focused stocks delivered 19% revenue growth in 4QFY26, a modest figure that belies the two-speed story: the rural cohort's growth was dragged lower by a few commodity-linked names masking genuine volume recovery in FMCG rural distribution.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Urban stocks revenue growth jumped to 61% YoY
charts.commentary: Urban stocks surged to 61% revenue growth — a massive spike driven by base effects and concentrated in a few large urban consumption names; at face value this appears impressive but the base distortion makes the number misleading as a cycle read.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Rural stocks Ebitda growth rose to 58% YoY
charts.commentary: Rural EBITDA growth of 58% YoY was the standout performer across all cohorts, driven by a recovery in agri-input, agrochemical and rural FMCG margins — a bullish signal for rural-exposed consumer staples names heading into the monsoon season.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Urban stocks Ebitda growth fell to 16% YoY
charts.commentary: Despite 61% revenue growth, urban EBITDA grew only 16% — a dramatic revenue-to-EBITDA conversion failure indicating severe cost pressures or mix effects in urban consumption, and a warning sign for premium urban discretionary valuations.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Rural stocks PBT growth saw meaningful uptick
charts.commentary: Rural PBT growth saw a meaningful uptick in 4QFY26, closing the gap with urban peers and reinforcing CLSA's preference for rural consumption plays over urban cyclicals in the current macro environment.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Urban stocks PBT growth moderated to 14% YoY
charts.commentary: Urban PBT growth moderated to 14% despite high revenue growth, with the chart showing significant volatility in prior quarters; the widening gap between revenue and profit growth for urban stocks is a key earnings quality risk for FY27.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Change in net sales compared to the start of the earnings season for our estimates
charts.commentary: Net sales estimates were revised up most sharply for Consumer Discretionary and Telecom while Oil & Gas (State) saw meaningful cuts during the earnings season; the divergence highlights that sector-level earnings momentum is bifurcated, not broad-based.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Change in Ebitda compared to the start of the earnings season for our estimates
charts.commentary: EBITDA estimate changes show Consumer Discretionary and Software receiving upgrades while the CLSA Coverage Universe aggregate and Oil & Gas (State) saw the largest downgrades — confirming that the headline universe EBITDA cut was concentrated in a few sectors.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Change in Ebitda margin compared to the start of the earnings season for our estimates
charts.commentary: EBITDA margin estimate changes show Banks and Oil & Gas (Private) receiving the largest upgrades while Oil & Gas (State), Cement, and Metals saw the largest margin downgrades since the season started — energy and materials remain the key swing factors for index-level margins.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Change in PBT compared to the start of the earnings season for our estimates
charts.commentary: PBT estimate revisions show Consumer Staples and Software as the brightest spots for upgrades while Oil & Gas (State), Cement and Metals absorbed the deepest cuts; the chart for FY28 shows a similar negative skew, suggesting multi-year earnings risk in cyclical sectors.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Bloomberg consensus EPS upgrades/(downgrades)
charts.commentary: Bloomberg consensus Nifty EPS saw net downgrades of -15.5% and -20.55pp during the 4QFY26 reporting season for FY27 and FY28 respectively — the largest cut cycles in several years, confirming that the broader street is catching up to CLSA's already-cautious stance.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Our Nifty EPS estimate is above consensus for FY27
charts.commentary: CLSA's FY27 Nifty EPS estimate sits above Bloomberg consensus (premium of 0.2) while CLSA is below consensus for FY28 (discount of -1.9), suggesting CLSA sees near-term resilience but expects cuts to persist into FY28 as the cycle matures.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: CLSA Nifty EPS downgraded for FY27/FY28 during the 4QFY26
charts.commentary: CLSA cut its own Nifty EPS estimates for both FY27 and FY28 during the 4QFY26 season, with the FY28 cut being larger — a candid admission that the multi-year earnings recovery is slower than the house had modelled.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Consensus upgrade/(downgrade) of the sector's FY27/FY28 EPS during 4QFY26
charts.commentary: State-owned oil & gas and metals saw the largest FY27 consensus upgrades while Consumer Discretionary, Oil & Gas Private, and Pharmaceuticals absorbed the deepest cuts — the sector dispersion in EPS revisions is wide, underpinning CLSA's selective stock-picking stance rather than a broad market call.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Nifty constituent EPS growth (Cap - FY28 over FY26) versus the valuation premium/(discount) to its average (%)
charts.commentary: The scatter plot maps Nifty constituents by two-year EPS CAGR versus valuation premium/discount to historical averages, identifying quadrant winners (high growth + below-average valuation, e.g. TATACONS, APVL) and stocks to avoid (low growth + premium valuation); it serves as CLSA's key stock selection framework for the current earnings-cut environment.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Top contributors to FY28 PAT over FY26 PAT (as a percentage of total change in PAT) and their respective Nifty weights (%)
charts.commentary: HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles are the three largest contributors to FY28 PAT growth over FY26, each contributing over 8% of the total PAT increment. The chart highlights that the market's FY28 earnings recovery is heavily concentrated in a handful of names — financials and select cyclicals — implying index EPS is vulnerable if any of these beat/miss materially.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Good 4Q but EPS cuts continue
charts.chart_title: Nifty stocks FY27/28 net profit comparison: our estimate versus consensus
charts.commentary: The scatter maps CLSA's FY27 and FY28 EPS estimates against consensus, revealing that CLSA is meaningfully below consensus on several large-caps (ONGC, Indraprastha Gas, MARN, ADNSE) while above on a few (MSL, HDFC Life). The cluster of names where CLSA sits below consensus on both years signals persistent top-down EPS cut risk for the Nifty.

charts.report_title: India Autos, May-2026 volumes - EVs pick up, MHCVs slow down
charts.chart_title: Fig. 10: MSIL – discounts trend
charts.commentary: MSIL's absolute discount (INR, bar) and discount as % of ASP (line) have trended up from lows in FY22–23, with % ASP back near 4–5% by early FY27, indicating that competitive pressure and softer demand for some models is nudging Maruti to increase retail support — a watch item for near-term margin trajectory.

charts.report_title: India Autos, May-2026 volumes - EVs pick up, MHCVs slow down
charts.chart_title: Fig. 16: Commodity Cost Index for PVs
charts.analyst_caption: Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P., Nomura research
charts.commentary: The PV commodity cost index (% of ASP) has declined materially from its FY22–23 peak and is trending near recent lows, providing a structural tailwind to PV OEM margins even as discounts inch up — net margin expansion for well-positioned OEMs like M&M and Hyundai remains a live thesis.

charts.report_title: India Autos, May-2026 volumes - EVs pick up, MHCVs slow down
charts.chart_title: Fig. 17: Commodity Cost Index for 2Ws
charts.analyst_caption: Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P., Nomura research

charts.report_title: India Autos, May-2026 volumes - EVs pick up, MHCVs slow down
charts.chart_title: Fig. 18: Commodity Cost Index for CVs
charts.analyst_caption: Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P., Nomura research

charts.report_title: India Financials - India Financial Daily, 2 June 2026
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 1 - System liquidity in surplus territory as Rs454mn as of 1-Jun
charts.commentary: System liquidity has moved into surplus territory at Rs454bn as of 1 June, reversing the deficit seen earlier in 2026. Surplus conditions ease near-term funding pressure for banks and support transmission of the RBI rate cut cycle.

charts.report_title: India Financials - India Financial Daily, 2 June 2026
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 5 - Banks' loan growth has risen over the past few months, but loan+investment growth is in line with deposit growth
charts.commentary: The multi-series chart shows loan growth recovering to ~16% YoY while deposit growth holds at ~12%, with the combined loan+investment line tracking closely to deposits. The gap between loan and deposit growth bears watching as a potential funding constraint if deposits do not accelerate.

charts.report_title: India Financials - India Financial Daily, 2 June 2026
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 6 - Bank credit growth was stable to 16% YoY on 15-May-26
charts.commentary: Bank credit growth stabilised at 16% YoY as of mid-May 2026, consistent with the trend of the past few months; sustained double-digit credit growth is supportive of NII expansion for lenders but must be matched by deposit mobilisation.

charts.report_title: India Financials - India Financial Daily, 2 June 2026
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 7 - Bank deposit growth stood at 12% YoY on 15-May-26
charts.commentary: Deposit growth at 12% YoY continues to lag loan growth by ~400bp, implying banks must compete more aggressively for liabilities — a structural headwind for margin expansion in the near term.

charts.report_title: India Financials - India Financial Daily, 2 June 2026
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 8 - Credit/deposits ratio stood at c.82%
charts.commentary: The credit-to-deposit (CD) ratio has stabilised around 82%, having risen sharply from post-Covid lows; a high and sticky CD ratio limits incremental lending capacity and keeps deposit pricing competitive, a mild negative for NIMs.

charts.report_title: India Financials - India Financial Daily, 2 June 2026
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 9 - Investment/deposits ratio stood at c.27%
charts.commentary: The investment-to-deposit ratio at ~27% reflects the statutory liquidity buffer maintained by banks; a stable-to-declining ratio would indicate banks are preferring loan deployment over SLR holdings, consistent with the observed credit growth pickup.

charts.report_title: India Economics - EcoTracker_ April 2026
charts.chart_title: Figure 1: EAT suggests real GVA growth moderated to 7.8% in Apr-26
charts.analyst_caption: Source: RBI, CSO, Various national sources, CEIC, CLSA
charts.commentary: CLSA's EAT (Economic Activity Tracker) points to India's real GVA growth moderating to 7.8% YoY in April 2026, with a 3-month moving average confirming the sequential deceleration. The softer reading reflects weakness in the industrial sector and slower consumption, signalling a modest near-term growth headwind.

charts.report_title: India Economics - EcoTracker_ April 2026
charts.chart_title: Figure 2: ...it remained strong at 8.9% YoY in 4QFY26
charts.analyst_caption: Source: RBI, CSO, Various national sources, CEIC, CLSA
charts.commentary: Official GVA and CLSA's EAT both confirm a solid 4QFY26 print of ~8.9% YoY, well above trend, which anchors the FY26 full-year estimate at an elevated level. This back-end strength means the base effect will be meaningfully harder in 1QFY27, raising the bar for any positive growth surprise.

charts.report_title: India Economics - EcoTracker_ April 2026
charts.chart_title: Figure 3: Industrial sector growth eased to a 14-month slowest in Apr-26...
charts.analyst_caption: Source: RBI, CSO, Various national sources, CEIC, CLSA. Note: *Including construction sector
charts.commentary: Industrial sector EAT decelerated to a 14-month low in April 2026, with the 3-month moving average rolling over. The weakness is broad-based across manufacturing sub-indices, pointing to a cyclical soft patch that could weigh on capital-goods and industrials earnings in 1QFY27.

charts.report_title: India Economics - EcoTracker_ April 2026
charts.chart_title: Figure 4: ...after a very strong performance in 4QFY26
charts.analyst_caption: Source: RBI, CSO, Various national sources, CEIC, CLSA. Note: *Including construction sector
charts.commentary: Official industrial GVA hit 8.2% YoY in 4QFY26 vs CLSA's EAT estimate, confirming very robust quarter-end momentum. The sharp reversal implied by the April reading suggests a significant step-down in 1QFY27 industrial growth is likely, which may disappoint consensus expectations.

charts.report_title: India Economics - EcoTracker_ April 2026
charts.chart_title: Figure 5: Services' EAT growth was at a 3-month high in Apr-26...
charts.analyst_caption: Source: RBI, CSO, Various national sources, CEIC, CLSA
charts.commentary: Services EAT rebounded to a 3-month high in April 2026, offering a partial offset to industrial weakness. Resilient services activity — underpinned by strong auto sales and passenger traffic — supports a services-led growth composition that favors financials and consumer discretionary over industrials.

charts.report_title: India Economics - EcoTracker_ April 2026
charts.chart_title: Figure 6: ...and it is estimated to have grown 8.4% in 4QFY26
charts.analyst_caption: Source: RBI, CSO, Various national sources, CEIC, CLSA
charts.commentary: CLSA estimates services sector real GVA at 8.4% YoY for 4QFY26, broadly in line with the official print, confirming durable services momentum. This sustained outperformance reinforces the structural shift toward services-driven GDP and supports the premium valuation commanded by high-quality services franchises.

charts.report_title: India Economics - EcoTracker_ April 2026
charts.chart_title: Figure 7: Consumption growth has moderated sequentially in Apr-26...
charts.analyst_caption: Source: RBI, CSO, Various national sources, CEIC, CLSA
charts.commentary: Private consumption (PFCE) growth moderated in April 2026 after a strong run, with the 3-month moving average beginning to flatten. Sequential deceleration in consumption suggests that rural demand recovery and urban income tailwinds may be losing momentum, a watch-point for consumer staples and discretionary stocks.

charts.report_title: India Economics - EcoTracker_ April 2026
charts.chart_title: Figure 8: ...after a largely stable good growth in 4QFY26
charts.analyst_caption: Source: RBI, CSO, Various national sources, CEIC, CLSA
charts.commentary: Consumption growth held at ~6.9% YoY in 4QFY26 per CLSA's EAT versus official estimates, indicating stable but not accelerating household demand. A consumption growth rate near 7% is supportive of earnings for consumer-facing companies but leaves limited scope for upward earnings revisions absent a fresh demand catalyst.

charts.report_title: India Economics - EcoTracker_ April 2026
charts.chart_title: Figure 9: Investment growth remained stable in Apr-26, albeit soft...
charts.analyst_caption: Source: RBI, CSO, Various national sources, CEIC, CLSA
charts.commentary: Investment (GFCF) growth stayed positive but soft in April 2026, with the monthly trend showing little sequential acceleration. Muted capex momentum — despite government push — limits near-term upside for capital goods and infrastructure-linked names and keeps the recovery story dependent on private sector confidence.

charts.report_title: India Economics - EcoTracker_ April 2026
charts.chart_title: Figure 10: ...though it stayed strong at 7.6% in 4QFY26
charts.analyst_caption: Source: RBI, CSO, Various national sources, CEIC, CLSA
charts.commentary: CLSA's investment growth EAT of 8.0% aligns closely with the 7.6% official 4QFY26 figure, validating the tracker's predictive accuracy. Sustained high-single-digit investment growth through FY26 is a positive structural signal but is already partially in consensus, limiting incremental re-rating potential for capex-linked sectors.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 2 - Cost of rewards on credit cards has risen
charts.commentary: Reward costs as a percentage of credit-card transaction value have risen visibly over the recent period, underpinning the sector-wide decision to tighten benefit structures; the moderation in reward spend is a direct lever for recovering basis points of card-segment profitability.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 6 - Higher fees are charged on credit/ debit cards, while UPI to continue to remain free
charts.commentary: A fee-structure bar chart comparing interchange/MDR on credit cards, debit cards and UPI (zero); the structural fee advantage of UPI keeps it the dominant low-cost channel, while card issuers must rely on reward rationalisation rather than fee increases to improve economics.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 7 - UPI trx value has steadily expanded over the past few years, crossing Rs300tn in FY26
charts.commentary: UPI transaction value crossed ₹300 trillion in FY26, with growth in value (YoY %) remaining robust — the scale of UPI underscores the competitive pressure on credit-card spends volumes and validates issuers' focus on growing the higher-value card-spend ticket rather than chasing volume.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 8 - Growth moderated in credit card transaction value.
charts.commentary: Credit card transaction value (₹tn) grew steadily through FY21–FY26 but YoY growth rates have moderated sharply from >40% in FY22 to low single digits in FY26, reflecting both a high base and demand softness that makes reward-cost rationalisation critical to maintaining segment ROE.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 9 - ...while debit card transaction values declined
charts.commentary: Debit card transaction values have declined in absolute terms as UPI cannibalises usage; this structural shift means banks can no longer cross-subsidise card economics with debit-card fee income, increasing pressure on credit-card profitability.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 10 - Overall Credit cards issuance has trended downward over the past two years.
charts.commentary: Net new credit-card additions (mn, RHS) have declined for the past two years, falling from ~35–40mn gross issuances toward ~20mn as banks tighten underwriting to protect credit quality; lower card growth limits the revenue offset to reward-cost cuts.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 11 - ...hence growth in cards o/s has been weak
charts.commentary: Cards outstanding growth (YoY %) has slowed to low single digits through early CY26, confirming that the industry is in a consolidation phase; steady-state profitability must therefore come from better economics per card rather than volume growth.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 12 - Revolver mix declined 200bps in FY26 to 27% as.
charts.commentary: The revolving-credit mix on SBI Cards fell 200bps to ~27% in FY26, reducing the proportion of high-yield balances; with fewer revolvers, interest income softens and reward-cost efficiency becomes more important to defending overall card-segment returns.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 13 - ...growth in revolver value has moderated
charts.commentary: SBI Cards revolver value growth has moderated sharply, compressing net interest income from this high-margin pool and amplifying the need for fee/reward-cost management to sustain PAT margins.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 14 - Cost of rewards on credit cards has risen
charts.commentary: Reward points utilised as a percentage of credit card transaction value rose from 23bps (FY22–FY24) to 28bps in FY25, confirming that cardholders were redeeming aggressively — the catalyst for issuers to now cap and reduce reward programmes to claw back these economics.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 19 - Growth in SBI Cards' EMI book remained muted in recent years
charts.commentary: SBI Cards' EMI book (₹bn) stagnated at ~₹160–195bn over FY22–FY26, with the EMI share of AUM declining as a percentage — a missed growth opportunity in the higher-yielding EMI segment that, if recovered, could support net interest income even as revolver mix slips.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 21 - Credit card spending slowed over past year.
charts.commentary: Industry credit-card spends (₹tn) with YoY growth rate overlay shows a clear deceleration through CY25–CY26, confirming that volume growth cannot compensate for economics pressures — making reward-cost reduction the primary path to profitability recovery.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 22 - ...while cards u/s growth remained steady
charts.commentary: Cards-in-force (mn) maintained steady sequential growth even as spend growth slowed, implying average spends per card have compressed — a structural headwind to fee income that underscores the importance of higher-quality, higher-spending cardholders over mass issuance.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 23 - HDFC & SBI gained share in card spending over FY23-25, while...
charts.commentary: Market-share breakdown of credit card spending across HDFC, ICICI, SBI, Axis and others over Mar-21 to Mar-25 shows HDFC and SBI gaining share — HDFC's dominant position (>29%) gives it scale to absorb reward-cost cuts without proportionate volume loss.

charts.report_title: India Financials - Credit Card Issuers Tighten Rewards & Spends To Support Prof
charts.chart_title: Exhibit 24 - ...cards u/s for both banks saw a modest change over the same period
charts.commentary: Cards outstanding market-share comparison for the same period shows more modest shifts versus spending share, implying HDFC and SBI are winning higher-spending customers — a quality mix improvement that partially offsets the revenue headwind from reward tightening.

charts.chart_title: Exhibit 30 - In 3QFY26, NTC share declined in PLs, while remaining stable in Credit cards
charts.commentary: New-to-credit (NTC) borrower share fell in personal loans in 3QFY26 but remained stable for credit cards (~4%), suggesting card issuers have already tightened underwriting toward established borrowers — a credit-quality positive that reduces future credit-cost risk for the card segment.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Trade baskets for a dry season
charts.chart_title: Figure 1 Southern Oscillation Index
charts.analyst_caption: Notes: Figures less than 0 denote El Nino conditions while above 0 denotes La Nina. Source: CLSA, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
charts.commentary: The Southern Oscillation Index shows the current El Nino episode is well established (negative reading), with only a handful of such episodes in the last 25 years; historically El Nino correlates with deficient Indian monsoon rainfall, the core risk CLSA is stress-testing in this report.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Trade baskets for a dry season
charts.chart_title: Figure 3 Actual rainfall during El Nino and non-El Nino years
charts.analyst_caption: Notes: Red represents El Nino years having deficient rainfall; 2026 is IMD's rainfall forecast. Source: CLSA, CME, IMD
charts.commentary: The bar chart confirms that El Nino years (red bars) cluster below the 90% LPA deficiency threshold far more often than neutral or La Nina years; the 2026 IMD forecast of ~105% LPA is at the upper end of the El Nino distribution, suggesting buffers exist but complacency is unwarranted.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Trade baskets for a dry season
charts.chart_title: Figure 4 Reservoir levels as % of live capacity
charts.commentary: Current reservoir levels at 30.4% of live capacity are materially above the 12-27% range seen in pre-drought years this century, providing a significant buffer for domestic water supply and Kharif crop sowing even if the 2026 monsoon disappoints.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Trade baskets for a dry season
charts.chart_title: Figure 5 Food production growth vs rainfall
charts.commentary: The dual-axis chart shows that YoY food production declines reliably coincide with sub-90% LPA rainfall years; given 2026 IMD forecasts 105% LPA, a production shock appears unlikely, but a downside miss could quickly transmit to food inflation — a key macro watch-point.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Trade baskets for a dry season
charts.chart_title: Figure 6 India's food grain stock
charts.commentary: India's April 2026 foodgrain stock of 112MT is at an all-time high, roughly double the levels seen in prior drought years, providing a strong government buffer against retail food price spikes even in a deficient monsoon scenario.

charts.report_title: India strategy - Trade baskets for a dry season
charts.chart_title: Figure 7 Nifty's absolute and relative performance during Jun-Sep period of each El Nino year
charts.commentary: In three out of five El Nino episodes the Nifty delivered positive absolute returns in Jun-Sep and outperformed MSCI EM in four of five, suggesting the broader market has historically shrugged off dry-season risk — the stock-selection opportunity lies in identifying sector divergences within this broadly constructive picture.
